escena: SCENE (staged editorial photograph, freeze-frame at 1/8000 s, a real content studio in Santiago at dusk, warm wood table, NO fantasy, NO glowing effects): a content strategist wearing the deep navy EFEONCE BOMBER (deep navy, never royal blue) stands behind a long wooden editorial table, his face centred at about 58% of the frame width and at about 36% of the frame height (NOT higher), his head about one fifth of the frame height, framed from the waist up, camera about two meters away at chest height, 85mm f/2.8. He has just slapped both palms down on ONE printed master article lying on the table, and at that instant the whole content plan around it LEAPS into the air: printed article pages, storyboard frames of a short video, index cards with headlines, a few instant photos of a podcast mic and a camera, loose sticky notes — all FROZEN mid-air in an upward burst around his hands and shoulders, every sheet sharp and perfectly still, some catching the light. He looks straight into the lens with a quick, delighted grin, eyes sharp. The ONE color accent of the frame is TEAL (#36C8BF): the sticky notes and the cover of the master article are teal, nothing else is teal. The BLUE of the frame is carried ONLY by his deep navy Efeonce bomber; there is NO monitor, NO screen and NO blue panel anywhere in the room; the ONLY light is a small daylight LED panel standing LOW on the table at the right edge of the frame, at hand height, the brightest thing in the frame, raking across his hands, the flying pages and the right side of his face, while the far side of his face falls into open shadow with the nose shadow legible on his cheek; every other lamp in the room is switched OFF, nothing warm, no amber glow. His face, both hands and the burst of pages all fit inside a circle centred at about 58% of the width and one third of the height, with air around them; nothing important sits in the upper-left of that circle. The LEFT 40% of the frame and the lower-left quarter are calm: the dim end of the table and an unlit plain wall, no pages, no objects, no people. Natural white balance, no color grade, completely unbranded except his bomber.
